questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my spoken korean and therefore picked the university that is most commonly known for having a focus on spoken korean.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to COVID-19 the entire academic part of my exchange was conducted online.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinator at Sogang University sent out plenty of information before I even arrived in Korea.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any particular assistance myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was easy to get in touch with the coordinator. Everything in terms of orientation was cancelled due to COVID.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly easily as we found ours through airbnb. That way you also avoid contracts and so on.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is going to be substantially more expensive than the university dormitory, however if you want to cook your own food and not deal with curfews then off campus housing is far better.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sogangs dormitory does not have a shared kitchen space nor do they offer single rooms. Due to these reasons it was never an option for me to live there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: To be quite honest i don't really remember.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the international students office by email if you required any help or address a large pdf that was distributed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: You had to dig through a 70+ page document to find the actual procedure of how to apply for clases and it still wasn't completely clear how to do it. You have to click the name of the class specifically and not just any random place when you find it during the registration period.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to read the application process over several times so you're sure where to click and don't end up missing out on a class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My communication class is an absolute 1, i cannot recommend intro to communication less. I would give their KAP200 program a 4.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of the communication class was reminiscent of a college prep teacher cramming your brain with nothing but theories that are then not elaborated on in a significant manner. There was no reading for the classes and all you had to do was take notes during class from powerpoints that the professor refuses to send you because that is all of his material. 

KAP200 was an intense 4 hours a day of korean lessons that definitely improved my korean skills quite significantly.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The level of teaching that was displayed by my communication professor telegraphed that it was quite poor. But perhaps they have more talented professors on staff.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intro to Communication. 
KLEC KAP200 level 3.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
KLEC KAP200. 
The program is very intense as it only goes on for 10 weeks, but the teachers are very good at what they do. It is divided into 3 blocks every day, 1 hour of Academic writing, 2 hours of Oral korean and 1 hour of reading and listening. It's well structured.

questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go sighteseeing at historical sights even if you think you may find it boring, it is fascinating to see how modern culture is shaped by the past.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have been to korea many times before and therefore had no issues adjusting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Only been on exchange during COVID so unfortunately no.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They're very helpful people and will go quite far to make sure you get the help you need.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure you do your research about where you want to live and decide as early as possible. 
Pick your classes beforehand and have a few backups as class registration is very competitive and goes really fast. 
Make sure your insurance covers enough as Sogang requires you have a pretty extensive insurance.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not in particular.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I managed to genuinely improve my korean, that made it worthwhile for me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting my Foreigner Registration Card. Due to COVID booking a time to go and apply was extremely restricted and you had to book months in advance.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
